title: P46 (Chester Beatty II): 2 Corinthians 1:1-2:1 (fols. 61r-62r)
source: P46 (Chester Beatty Biblical Papyrus II, Chester Beatty Library, Dublin): photographs as published in the INTF New Testament Virtual Manuscript Room; Greek from the INTF NTVMR transcription of P46; English from the King James Version
description: 2 Corinthians 1:1-2:1 in P46, the papyrus codex of Paul's letters copied around 200: fols. 61r-62r, each page with its photograph, the Greek transcription and the King James Version.
introduction:
P46 is a papyrus codex of the letters of Paul copied in Egypt around 200, the oldest surviving collection of Paul's letters. 86 of its 104 leaves survive: 56 in the Chester Beatty Library, Dublin (Biblical Papyrus II, published by Frederic Kenyon in 1934-1937) and 30 in the University of Michigan Library, Ann Arbor (P.Mich. inv. 6238, published by Henry Sanders in 1935). The letters run in the order Romans, Hebrews, 1 and 2 Corinthians, Ephesians, Galatians, Philippians, Colossians and 1 Thessalonians; the first seven leaves (Romans 1:1-5:17) and the end of the book are lost. Hebrews standing after Romans, and the doxology of Romans (16:25-27) standing after 15:33, are among its best-known features.

Each section below is one page side: the holding library's photograph, the NTVMR diplomatic transcription line by line, and the King James Version of every verse that has text on the page. The lower lines of many leaves are lost; the transcribers' restorations are in square brackets.

This entry covers fols. 61r-62r (2 Corinthians 1:1-2:1).
translator_notes: Greek: the NTVMR diplomatic transcription, line by line as on the papyrus. Square brackets enclose letters that are lost or illegible and were supplied by the transcribers; a dot under a letter marks it as uncertain; [...] marks a gap. Nomina sacra and numerals keep the scribe's overline. Spelling is the scribe's (no accents or breathings). Words broken at a line end stay broken as on the papyrus. Corrections are not shown: the text is the first hand.

English: the King James Version (1611), whole verses, for every verse that has text on the page. A verse that begins on one page and ends on the next is given in full on both. The KJV translates a later form of the Greek text, so its wording does not always match the papyrus; material differences (such as verses the papyrus does not have) are noted in the section.

translation.text: <sup>1:1</sup>Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, unto the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints which are in all Achaia: <sup>2</sup>Grace be to you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ. <sup>3</sup>Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort; <sup>4</sup>Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God. <sup>5</sup>For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ. <sup>6</sup>And whether we be afflicted, it is for your consolation and salvation, which is effectual in the enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer: or whether we be comforted, it is for your consolation and salvation. <sup>7</sup>And our hope of you is stedfast, knowing, that as ye are partakers of the sufferings, so shall ye be also of the consolation. <sup>8</sup>For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life:
translation.scan_note: Chester Beatty Library photograph T0005051.jpg (https://ntmss.info/images/webfriendly/10046/T0005051.jpg), linked to NTVMR page 1030 (folio 61r) in NTVMR's page index. 1:8 continues on the next page. The page also carries a book title, shown in italics in the Greek (προς κορινθιους β̅); the KJV has no English for it. Checked on the image: the scribe's page number ριη (118) at the head of the page, continuing the sequence of the neighbouring pages; the disc on the frame reads ‹P. II 61R›.

translation.text: <sup>1:8</sup>For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life: <sup>9</sup>But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead: <sup>10</sup>Who delivered us from so great a death, and doth deliver: in whom we trust that he will yet deliver us; <sup>11</sup>Ye also helping together by prayer for us, that for the gift bestowed upon us by the means of many persons thanks may be given by many on our behalf. <sup>12</sup>For our rejoicing is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God, we have had our conversation in the world, and more abundantly to you-ward. <sup>13</sup>For we write none other things unto you, than what ye read or acknowledge; and I trust ye shall acknowledge even to the end; <sup>14</sup>As also ye have acknowledged us in part, that we are your rejoicing, even as ye also are ours in the day of the Lord Jesus. <sup>15</sup>And in this confidence I was minded to come unto you before, that ye might have a second benefit;

Checked on the image: the scribe's page number ριθ (119) at the head of the page, continuing the sequence of the neighbouring pages.

translation.text: <sup>1:16</sup>And to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia unto you, and of you to be brought on my way toward Judaea. <sup>17</sup>When I therefore was thus minded, did I use lightness? or the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, that with me there should be yea yea, and nay nay? <sup>18</sup>But as God is true, our word toward you was not yea and nay. <sup>19</sup>For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, even by me and Silvanus and Timotheus, was not yea and nay, but in him was yea. <sup>20</sup>For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us. <sup>21</sup>Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God; <sup>22</sup>Who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts. <sup>23</sup>Moreover I call God for a record upon my soul, that to spare you I came not as yet unto Corinth. <sup>24</sup>Not for that we have dominion over your faith, but are helpers of your joy: for by faith ye stand. <sup>2:1</sup>But I determined this with myself, that I would not come again to you in heaviness.
